+# A degree-seven counterexample to the subspace-product conjecture
+
+## Abstract
+
+The degree-seven field Q[X]/(X^7-2) refutes Aliabadi's subspace-product lower bound: there are no proper nontrivial intermediate fields, but two five-dimensional subspaces have product span of dimension at most seven, below the proposed lower bound nine.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Multiplicative field translates).**
+
+$$\forall (K:Type), \forall (L:Type), [\operatorname{Field}\left(K\right)], [\operatorname{Field}\left(L\right)], [\operatorname{Algebra}\left(K, L\right)], \forall (a:L), \forall (M:\operatorname{IntermediateField}\left(K, L\right)), \operatorname{translate}\left(a, M\right) = \operatorname{map}\left(\operatorname{mulLeft}\left(K, a\right), M\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.translate` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Mohsen Aliabadi (2025). *Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II*. DOI: [10.7151/dmgaa.1461](https://doi.org/10.7151/dmgaa.1461). URL: <https://www.dmgaa.uz.zgora.pl/publish/pdf.php?doi=1461>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+K and L are arbitrary fields equipped with a K-algebra structure on L. M is an actual intermediate field. Its underlying K-subspace is mapped by the K-linear map x mapped to a times x. Thus translate(a,M) consists exactly of the products am for m in M. The scalar a may be zero.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The full intermediate-field premise).**
+
+$$\forall (K:Type), \forall (L:Type), [\operatorname{Field}\left(K\right)], [\operatorname{Field}\left(L\right)], [\operatorname{Algebra}\left(K, L\right)], \forall (A:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \forall (B:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \operatorname{intersectionPremise}\left(A, B\right) \Leftrightarrow \forall (a:L), \forall (b:L), \forall (M:\operatorname{IntermediateField}\left(K, L\right)), \left(\operatorname{bot}\left(\right) < M \land \left(M < \operatorname{top}\left(\right) \land \operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(K, M\right)\right)\right) \Rightarrow \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, \operatorname{inf}\left(\operatorname{translate}\left(a, M\right), A\right)\right)+\operatorname{finrank}\left(K, \operatorname{inf}\left(\operatorname{translate}\left(b, M\right), B\right)\right) \le \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, M\right)+1$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.intersectionPremise` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Mohsen Aliabadi (2025). *Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II*. DOI: [10.7151/dmgaa.1461](https://doi.org/10.7151/dmgaa.1461). URL: <https://www.dmgaa.uz.zgora.pl/publish/pdf.php?doi=1461>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The predicate quantifies over every a and b in L and every finite-dimensional intermediate field M that properly contains K and is properly contained in L. Bottom represents the embedded base field and top represents L. Intersections are submodule infima; finrank is dimension over K, and finrank(K,M) is the degree [M:K]. The full ambient field is excluded from this premise.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The whole original conjecture).**
+
+$$claim \Leftrightarrow \forall (K:Type), \forall (L:Type), [\operatorname{Field}\left(K\right)], [\operatorname{Field}\left(L\right)], [\operatorname{Algebra}\left(K, L\right)], \forall (A:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \forall (B:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \left(\operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(K, A\right) \land \left(\operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(K, B\right) \land \left(0 < \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, A\right) \land \left(0 < \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, B\right) \land \operatorname{intersectionPremise}\left(A, B\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) \Rightarrow \forall (S:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \forall (T:\operatorname{Submodule}\left(K, L\right)), \left(S \le A \land T \le B\right) \Rightarrow \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, S\right)+\operatorname{finrank}\left(K, T\right)-1 \le \operatorname{finrank}\left(K, \operatorname{span}\left(K, S T\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Mohsen Aliabadi (2025). *Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II*. DOI: [10.7151/dmgaa.1461](https://doi.org/10.7151/dmgaa.1461). URL: <https://www.dmgaa.uz.zgora.pl/publish/pdf.php?doi=1461>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+This is Conjecture 5.1 of arXiv:2309.14664v1-v3, section 5.1, and Conjecture 38 of the journal article, printed page 154. K and L range over fields with a K-algebra structure on L. A and B are arbitrary finite-dimensional K-subspaces of positive dimensions. S and T range over all K-subspaces of L contained in A and B respectively. No equality of dimensions, separability, infinite-extension condition, dimension-sum restriction, or cap by [L:K] is imposed. The notation span(K,ST) denotes the K-linear span of the actual pointwise product set {st : s in S, t in T}, as defined in section 2.2. The subtraction is natural-number subtraction; at zero-dimensional S and T this gives the same inequality as the ordinary integer interpretation.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The defining polynomial).**
+
+$$polynomial = X^{7}-2$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.polynomial` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The polynomial has rational coefficients. Its integer counterpart is monic and Eisenstein at the prime ideal generated by two: all lower coefficients are divisible by two and the constant coefficient is not divisible by four. Gauss's lemma transfers irreducibility to Q[X].
+
+**Definition 1.5 (The realized quotient field).**
+
+$$Extension = \operatorname{AdjoinRoot}\left(polynomial\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.Extension` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+AdjoinRoot is the actual quotient Q[X]/(X^7-2). Irreducibility supplies its field structure. Its canonical power basis has dimension seven, hence it is finite-dimensional over Q. The base-field map is the injective algebra map into this nontrivial field.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (The class of X).**
+
+$$alpha = \operatorname{root}\left(polynomial\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.alpha` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Alpha is the quotient class of X. The quotient-root identity gives alpha to the seventh power equal to two. The canonical basis is 1, alpha, alpha squared, through alpha to the sixth.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Nonconstant power spans).**
+
+$$\forall (n:\mathbb{N}), \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{span}\left(\mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{range}\left(\lambda (i:\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right))\mapsto alpha^{\operatorname{val}\left(i\right)+1}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.powerSpan` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each natural number n, powerSpan(n) is the span of the actual powers alpha through alpha to the n. Fin n indexes exponents i+1. For n at most six these are distinct entries of the quotient's power basis, so their span has dimension n and does not contain the constant basis vector 1. In particular powerSpan(5) is properly contained in powerSpan(6), and powerSpan(6) is proper in Extension.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (The realized countermodel certificate).**
+
+$$countermodel \Leftrightarrow \begin{aligned}\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{Q}, Extension\right) = 7, alpha^{7} = 2,\\\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right)\right) = 6, \operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(5\right)\right) = 5,\\\operatorname{powerSpan}\left(5\right) < \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right), \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right) < \operatorname{top}\left(\right),\\\neg 1 \in \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right), \neg 1 \in \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(5\right),\\\operatorname{intersectionPremise}\left(\operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right), \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(6\right)\right),\\\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{span}\left(\mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(5\right) \operatorname{powerSpan}\left(5\right)\right)\right) \le 7\end{aligned}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.countermodel` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Take A=B=powerSpan(6) and S=T=powerSpan(5). These have dimensions six and five, S is properly contained in A, A is proper in L, and 1 is absent from both. Prime extension degree seven makes every intermediate field bottom or top, so the full premise holds for every scalar pair. The actual span of products of S and T is a submodule of the seven-dimensional field; its dimension is therefore at most seven. This upper bound is sufficient, and no equality of that span with the field is asserted here.
+
+**Theorem 1.9 (The uncapped universal bound is false).**
+
+$$\neg claim$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/aliabadi-2025-matchability-subspace-product` (refuted) by `D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"aliabadi-2025-matchability-subspace-product","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Factorization/Galois/AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation.result","resolution_kind":"refuted"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Mohsen Aliabadi (2025). *Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II*. DOI: [10.7151/dmgaa.1461](https://doi.org/10.7151/dmgaa.1461). URL: <https://www.dmgaa.uz.zgora.pl/publish/pdf.php?doi=1461>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Applying the conjectured conclusion to the realized field and the selected subspaces would give a product-span dimension at least 5+5-1=9. The ambient field bounds that same dimension above by seven, a contradiction. The premise excludes the full intermediate field L and has no other intermediate field to test in prime degree. The refutation therefore concerns the whole original conjecture, including its full intermediate-field premise. It also uses strict proper subspaces, so replacing the ordinary containment symbols by strict containment does not remove this counterexample.
+

+import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.Basic
+import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.GaussLemma
+import Mathlib.RingTheory.AdjoinRoot
+import Mathlib.FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Basic
+import Mathlib.FieldTheory.KummerPolynomial
+import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Constructions
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Operations
+import Mathlib.Tactic
+
+/-! A prime-degree quotient field contradicts the uncapped universal product bound. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Factorization.Galois.AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation
+
+noncomputable section
+open Polynomial Module
+open scoped Pointwise
+
+/-- Multiplicative translate of an actual intermediate field, as a base-field subspace. -/
+def translate {K L : Type} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
+    (a : L) (M : IntermediateField K L) : Submodule K L :=
+  M.toSubalgebra.toSubmodule.map (LinearMap.mulLeft K a)
+
+/-- The premise quantifies over every scalar pair and every finite, nontrivial proper
+intermediate field. In particular the ambient field itself is excluded. -/
+def intersectionPremise {K L : Type} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
+    (A B : Submodule K L) : Prop :=
+  ∀ (a b : L) (M : IntermediateField K L), ⊥ < M → M < ⊤ →
+    FiniteDimensional K M →
+      finrank K ↥(translate a M ⊓ A) + finrank K ↥(translate b M ⊓ B) ≤
+        finrank K M + 1
+
+/-- Aliabadi's whole Conjecture 5.1 (journal Conjecture 38).
+The product is the span of the actual pointwise products in the extension field. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (K L : Type) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
+    (A B : Submodule K L), FiniteDimensional K A → FiniteDimensional K B →
+    0 < finrank K A → 0 < finrank K B → intersectionPremise A B →
+      ∀ (S T : Submodule K L), S ≤ A → T ≤ B →
+        finrank K S + finrank K T - 1 ≤
+          finrank K (Submodule.span K ((S : Set L) * (T : Set L)))
+
+/-- The rational polynomial defining the extension. -/
+abbrev polynomial : ℚ[X] := X ^ 7 - C 2
+
+private theorem polynomial_irreducible : Irreducible polynomial := by
+  let f : ℤ[X] := X ^ 7 - C 2
+  have hm : f.Monic := monic_X_pow_sub_C 2 (by decide)
+  have hp : (Ideal.span ({2} : Set ℤ)).IsPrime :=
+    (Ideal.span_singleton_prime (by norm_num : (2 : ℤ) ≠ 0)).2
+      (by norm_num : Prime (2 : ℤ))
+  have he : f.IsEisensteinAt (Ideal.span ({2} : Set ℤ)) := by
+    apply hm.isEisensteinAt_of_mem_of_notMem hp.ne_top
+    · intro i hi
+      have hi7 : i < 7 := by simpa only [f, natDegree_X_pow_sub_C] using hi
+      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
+      interval_cases i <;> norm_num [f, coeff_sub, coeff_X_pow, coeff_C]
+    · rw [Ideal.span_singleton_pow, Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
+      norm_num [f, coeff_sub, coeff_X_pow, coeff_C]
+  have hf : Irreducible f := he.irreducible hp hm.isPrimitive (by simp only [f, natDegree_X_pow_sub_C]; decide)
+  change Irreducible (X ^ 7 - C (2 : ℚ))
+  simpa only [f, Polynomial.map_sub, Polynomial.map_pow, Polynomial.map_X,
+    Polynomial.map_C, map_ofNat, Polynomial.map_ofNat] using
+    (Polynomial.IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast hm.isPrimitive).mp hf
+
+private instance polynomialFact : Fact (Irreducible polynomial) := ⟨polynomial_irreducible⟩
+
+/-- The actual quotient field Q[X]/(X^7-2). -/
+abbrev Extension := AdjoinRoot polynomial
+
+/-- The residue class of X in the quotient field. -/
+def alpha : Extension := AdjoinRoot.root polynomial
+
+private def powerBasis : PowerBasis ℚ Extension :=
+  AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' (monic_X_pow_sub_C 2 (by decide : 7 ≠ 0))
+
+private theorem powerBasis_dim : powerBasis.dim = 7 := by
+  simp [powerBasis, polynomial]
+
+private theorem powerBasis_gen : powerBasis.gen = alpha := rfl
+
+private instance extensionFinite : FiniteDimensional ℚ Extension := powerBasis.finite
+
+private theorem extension_degree : finrank ℚ Extension = 7 :=
+  powerBasis.finrank.trans powerBasis_dim
+
+/-- The span of alpha through alpha to the n, without the constant basis vector. -/
+def powerSpan (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℚ Extension :=
+  Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range fun i : Fin n => alpha ^ (i.val + 1))
+
+private def powerIndex {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 6) (i : Fin n) : Fin powerBasis.dim :=
+  ⟨i.val + 1, by rw [powerBasis_dim]; have := i.isLt; omega⟩
+
+private theorem powerIndex_injective {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 6) :
+    Function.Injective (powerIndex hn) := by
+  intro i j hij
+  apply Fin.ext
+  have := congrArg Fin.val hij
+  dsimp [powerIndex] at this
+  omega
+
+private theorem powerSpan_dim {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 6) : finrank ℚ (powerSpan n) = n := by
+  have h := powerBasis.basis.linearIndependent.comp (powerIndex hn) (powerIndex_injective hn)
+  have hli : LinearIndependent ℚ (fun i : Fin n => alpha ^ (i.val + 1)) := by
+    simpa only [Function.comp_def, powerBasis.basis_eq_pow, powerBasis_gen, powerIndex] using h
+  rw [powerSpan, finrank_span_eq_card hli, Fintype.card_fin]
+
+private theorem one_not_mem_powerSpan {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 6) :
+    (1 : Extension) ∉ powerSpan n := by
+  have heq : Set.range (fun i : Fin n => alpha ^ (i.val + 1)) =
+      powerBasis.basis '' Set.range (powerIndex hn) := by
+    rw [← Set.range_comp]
+    congr 1
+    funext i
+    simp only [Function.comp_apply, powerBasis.basis_eq_pow, powerBasis_gen, powerIndex]
+  intro h
+  have hzero : powerBasis.basis ⟨0, by rw [powerBasis_dim]; decide⟩ ∈
+      Submodule.span ℚ (powerBasis.basis '' Set.range (powerIndex hn)) := by
+    simpa [powerSpan, heq, powerBasis.basis_eq_pow, powerBasis_gen] using h
+  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := powerBasis.basis.self_mem_span_image.mp hzero
+  have := congrArg Fin.val hi
+  dsimp [powerIndex] at this
+  omega
+
+private theorem powerSpan_mono {n m : ℕ} (hnm : n ≤ m) : powerSpan n ≤ powerSpan m := by
+  apply Submodule.span_mono
+  rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
+  exact ⟨⟨i.val, lt_of_lt_of_le i.isLt hnm⟩, rfl⟩
+
+/-- The full realized certificate includes the proper subspaces and absence of 1.
+It asserts only the sufficient ambient upper bound for the actual product span. -/
+def countermodel : Prop :=
+  finrank ℚ Extension = 7 ∧ alpha ^ 7 = (2 : Extension) ∧
+  finrank ℚ (powerSpan 6) = 6 ∧ finrank ℚ (powerSpan 5) = 5 ∧
+  powerSpan 5 < powerSpan 6 ∧ powerSpan 6 < ⊤ ∧
+  (1 : Extension) ∉ powerSpan 6 ∧ (1 : Extension) ∉ powerSpan 5 ∧
+  intersectionPremise (powerSpan 6) (powerSpan 6) ∧
+  finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ
+    ((powerSpan 5 : Set Extension) * (powerSpan 5 : Set Extension))) ≤ 7
+
+private theorem countermodel_verified : countermodel := by
+  have hd6 := powerSpan_dim (by decide : 6 ≤ 6)
+  have hd5 := powerSpan_dim (by decide : 5 ≤ 6)
+  have hnot6 := one_not_mem_powerSpan (by decide : 6 ≤ 6)
+  have hnot5 := one_not_mem_powerSpan (by decide : 5 ≤ 6)
+  have hproper : powerSpan 6 < ⊤ :=
+    Submodule.lt_top_of_finrank_lt_finrank (by rw [hd6, extension_degree]; decide)
+  have hstrict : powerSpan 5 < powerSpan 6 :=
+    Submodule.lt_of_le_of_finrank_lt_finrank (powerSpan_mono (by decide : 5 ≤ 6))
+      (by rw [hd5, hd6]; decide)
+  have hprem : intersectionPremise (powerSpan 6) (powerSpan 6) := by
+    intro a b M hbot htop hfinite
+    letI : IsSimpleOrder (IntermediateField ℚ Extension) :=
+      IntermediateField.isSimpleOrder_of_finrank_prime ℚ Extension
+        (by rw [extension_degree]; decide)
+    rcases IsSimpleOrder.eq_bot_or_eq_top M with h | h
+    · exact False.elim (hbot.ne h.symm)
+    · exact False.elim (htop.ne h)
+  have hroot : alpha ^ 7 = (2 : Extension) := by
+    simpa only [alpha, polynomial, map_ofNat] using
+      (root_X_pow_sub_C_pow (K := ℚ) 7 2)
+  exact ⟨extension_degree, hroot, hd6, hd5, hstrict, hproper, hnot6, hnot5, hprem,
+    (Submodule.finrank_le _).trans_eq extension_degree⟩
+
+/-- The original universally quantified lower bound is false. -/
+theorem result : ¬ claim := by
+  intro h
+  obtain ⟨hdegree, hroot, hd6, hd5, hstrict, hproper, hnot6, hnot5, hprem, hproduct⟩ :=
+    countermodel_verified
+  have hlower := h ℚ Extension (powerSpan 6) (powerSpan 6)
+    (inferInstance) (inferInstance) (by omega) (by omega) hprem
+    (powerSpan 5) (powerSpan 5) hstrict.le hstrict.le
+  rw [hd5] at hlower
+  omega
+
+#print axioms result
+
+end
+end D5.S3.Factorization.Galois.AliabadiSubspaceProductRefutation

+
+# Subspace-product lower bound
+
+Discussiones Mathematicae General Algebra and Applications 45 (2025),
+135–157, section 5.1, Conjecture 38, printed page 154 / PDF page 20.
+The same statement is Conjecture 5.1 in arXiv:2309.14664v1, section 5.1,
+PDF page 14, and versions v2 and v3, PDF page 15.
+
+> Let K ⊂ L be a field extension and A,B ⊂ L be a K-subspace of L of
+> finite positive dimensions. Assume further that for every a,b ∈ L and
+> every nontrivial proper finite intermediate subfield K ⊂ M ⊊ L, we have
+> dim_K(aM ∩ A) + dim_K(bM ∩ B) ≤ [M:K] + 1.
+> Then for all K-subspaces S ⊂ A and T ⊂ B, the following holds
+> dim_K⟨ST⟩ ≥ dim_K S + dim_K T − 1.
+
+Section 2.2 (arXiv PDF page 7; journal printed page 143 / PDF page 9)
+defines ⟨ST⟩ as the K-linear span of the actual product set in L.
+A linear translate aM consists of the products am with m in M. Nontrivial
+means M properly contains K; proper means M differs from L. There is no
+restriction excluding finite ambient extensions or imposing a bound on
+the sum of the two subspace dimensions. Section 5.2 concerns a separate
+conjecture on Chowla subspaces.
+
+The equal-dimension and 1-not-in-B conditions in the introduction define
+linear matchability; Conjecture 38 does not invoke matchability as a
+hypothesis. It states finite positive dimensions for A and B, without
+requiring equality or that either space contain 1. The counterexample
+nevertheless has A=B, S=T, all four spaces exclude 1, and every indicated
+subspace containment is strict. The scalar quantifiers include zero.
+The word nontrivial excludes the base field, while proper excludes L.
+
+In the quotient Q[X]/(X^7−2), Eisenstein's criterion gives a field of
+degree seven. Prime degree excludes every intermediate field strictly
+between Q and the quotient. Take A=B=span(alpha,...,alpha^6) and
+S=T=span(alpha,...,alpha^5), where alpha is the class of X. The dimensions
+are six and five respectively, and these are proper subspaces with 1
+absent. The intermediate-field premise is therefore vacuous, whereas
+any product span has dimension at most seven. The proposed lower bound
+would require dimension at least nine. Exact equality of the product
+span with the whole field is unnecessary for this contradiction.
+
+The formal statement retains all field extensions, both finite positive
+dimensions, every scalar pair, every proper nontrivial finite intermediate
+field, and all pairs of contained subspaces. The selected proper subspaces
+also satisfy the strict reading of the source's ordinary subset symbols.

+# Aliabadi's uncapped subspace-product conjecture is false
+
+## Problem
+
+Mohsen Aliabadi, *Conditions for matchability in groups and field extensions II*,
+Discussiones Mathematicae General Algebra and Applications 45 (2025), 135–157,
+section 5.1, Conjecture 38, printed page 154 / PDF page 20, states:
+
+> Let $K\subset L$ be a field extension and $A,B\subset L$ be a $K$-subspace
+> of $L$ of finite positive dimensions. Assume further that for every
+> $a,b\in L$ and every nontrivial proper finite intermediate subfield
+> $K\subset M\subsetneq L$, we have
+>
+> $$\dim_K(aM\cap A)+\dim_K(bM\cap B)\le [M:K]+1.$$
+>
+> Then for all $K$-subspaces $S\subset A$ and $T\subset B$, the following holds
+>
+> $$\dim_K\langle ST\rangle\ge\dim_K S+\dim_K T-1.$$
+
+The same statement is Conjecture 5.1 in arXiv:2309.14664v1, PDF page 14,
+and v2/v3, PDF page 15. Section 2.2 defines the brackets as the $K$-linear
+span of the actual product set in $L$. The
+[source note](../Library/Factorization/aliabadi2025matchabilityii.md)
+records the primary versions, DOI and locators. The sole target is the
+whole original universal assertion. Preregistration:
+[#23409](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23409).
+
+### Statement correspondence
+
+| Source clause | Formal counterpart and witness |
+| --- | --- |
+| Arbitrary field extension $K\subset L$ | `claim` quantifies fields with a `K`-algebra structure on `L`. The witness is the actual field `AdjoinRoot (X^7-C 2)` over $\mathbb Q$, with the canonical injective algebra map and degree seven. |
+| Finite positive-dimensional $A,B$ | Both finite-dimensional hypotheses and both positive-finrank hypotheses occur in `claim`; $A=B=\operatorname{powerSpan}(6)$ has dimension six. |
+| Every $a,b\in L$, including zero | Both unrestricted scalar binders occur in `intersectionPremise`; `translate` maps the underlying submodule of $M$ by actual multiplication by the scalar. |
+| Every finite nontrivial proper intermediate field | `IntermediateField K L`, `⊥ < M`, `M < ⊤`, and `FiniteDimensional K M`. Neither endpoint is included. Prime degree proves that no witness field has such an $M$. |
+| Both intersection dimensions and $[M:K]+1$ | Submodule infima and finranks in `intersectionPremise` express the exact displayed inequality. No assumed certificate replaces it. |
+| Every allowed $S\subset A$, $T\subset B$ | `claim` quantifies all submodules with `S ≤ A` and `T ≤ B`, including the zero subspaces. The counterexample has both containments strict, so it also refutes the strict reading of the printed subset symbols. |
+| Actual $\langle ST\rangle$ | `Submodule.span K ((S : Set L) * (T : Set L))`, using field pointwise multiplication. |
+| Uncapped lower bound | `finrank K S + finrank K T - 1 ≤ finrank K (span ...)`; natural subtraction gives the same inequality truth value as integer subtraction, including zero dimensions. |
+| Whole-claim negation | The sole public theorem `result : ¬ claim` has no extra mathematical premise. |
+
+The matching definitions in the introduction use equal dimensions and
+$1\notin B$ when defining matchability. Conjecture 38 states neither
+matchability nor these conditions as an added premise. The witness
+nonetheless has $A=B$ and $S=T$, with $1$ absent from all four spaces.
+It also has $S<A<L$ and $T<B<L$. No assumption that a subspace contain
+$1$, that the ambient extension be infinite, or that the dimension sum
+be small is inserted. No ambient cap replaces the source conclusion.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Section 5.1 seeks a linear counterpart of the group product-set estimate
+used for sufficient matchability conditions. The conjecture would force
+expansion of every pair of contained subspaces from bounds on translated
+intermediate-field intersections. Its universal conclusion must also
+respect finite ambient dimension. A field of prime degree separates that
+obstruction from all the proper intermediate-field tests in the premise.
+
+## Gap
+
+The premise omits the ambient intermediate field $M=L$. In prime degree
+there is also no nontrivial proper intermediate field. Thus the premise
+places no restriction on $A$ and $B$ in this case, while the proposed
+conclusion can demand dimension larger than $[L:K]$. The obstruction
+persists for strict subspaces and for spaces avoiding $1$; it is not
+caused by choosing an endpoint or a zero-dimensional space.
+
+## Route
+
+Set $K=\mathbb Q$, $f=X^7-2$, $L=\mathbb Q[X]/(f)$ and let $\alpha$ be the
+class of $X$. Eisenstein at the prime ideal $(2)$ first proves the integer
+polynomial irreducible; its monicity gives primitiveness, and Gauss's
+lemma transfers irreducibility to $\mathbb Q[X]$. `AdjoinRoot` then supplies
+the field and its canonical algebra structure. Its power basis gives
+
+$$[L:\mathbb Q]=7,\qquad \alpha^7=2,\qquad
+1,\alpha,\alpha^2,\ldots,\alpha^6\text{ a basis}.$$
+
+Define
+
+$$A=B=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^6\},\qquad
+S=T=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^5\}.$$
+
+The selected powers are distinct basis entries. Their spans have
+dimensions six and five; the omitted constant entry proves $1$ is absent.
+The inclusion of the five powers among the six, together with their
+strict dimension inequality, proves $S<A$ and $T<B$. Dimension six is
+less than seven, so $A$ and $B$ are proper ambient subspaces.
+
+`IntermediateField.isSimpleOrder_of_finrank_prime` proves that every
+intermediate field is bottom or top. This discharges the full universal
+premise for every scalar pair and every finite nontrivial proper $M$.
+For the identical actual product span appearing in `claim`, the ambient
+finrank bound gives
+
+$$\dim_{\mathbb Q}\langle ST\rangle\le7<9=5+5-1.$$
+
+Applying the universal assertion to these fields and subspaces yields
+a contradiction. Exact equality $\langle ST\rangle=L$ is unnecessary and
+is not asserted as proved. The endpoint negates the whole original claim,
+not only a proposition about the selected parameter values.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+An omitted source condition excluding this finite extension or these
+subspaces, a different meaning of the printed intermediate-field range,
+or a failure of irreducibility, the actual quotient field, the power-basis
+dimensions, or the actual product-span bridge would invalidate the route.
+All four primary versions have the same quantified uncapped conclusion;
+the source conditions above are matched by the formal claim and witness.
+The optional exact product-span equality is outside the required argument.
